title: Return to the round boundary
statement: Let $m>0$, let $\delta:A\times\mathrm{Option}(\Gamma)\to A$, choose $a_0\in A$ and an acceptance predicate $\mathrm{acc}:A\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_m$ be nonempty words over $\Gamma$, and form $J$ by joining them in order with one blank symbol between consecutive words. Suppose a two-work-tape configuration $c$ is at the round's read control and, on tape 0, its cells at offsets $p$ from the head agree with the tape encoding of $J$ for every integer $p$ from $-1$ through $|J|$. Let $t$ be the first positive time at which the machine's control is either the read control or the exit control. Then $0<t\le 7(|J|+1)$; at every intermediate time $0<u<t$ its control is neither of these controls. At time $t$, the configuration agrees with $c$ except that its control is the exit control if $\mathrm{acc}$ accepts the state obtained by folding $\delta$ over $J$ from $a_0$, and otherwise is the read control; the head of tape 0 has moved by the sum of the lengths of the first $m-1$ words plus their separators in the accepted case, and by $|J|+1$ in the other case.
